items.title: Added /rewind support for resuming a conversation from before /clear was run

explanation.what_it_is: The /rewind command allows you to resume a conversation from a point before the /clear command was last run, effectively undoing the conversation reset.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change enables Claude Code users to recover conversation context that was previously lost when using /clear, making it easier to pick up where they left off.
how_to_use: Use /rewind to revert a conversation to its state before the last /clear command
Run /rewind immediately after /clear to resume the conversation from the previous point

items.title: Added sandbox.credentials setting to block sandboxed commands from reading credential files and secret environment variables

explanation.what_it_is: The sandbox.credentials setting is a new configuration option that prevents sandboxed commands from accessing credential files and secret environment variables.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change allows Claude Code users to better secure their sensitive information by restricting sandboxed commands from reading credentials and secrets.
how_to_use: Set sandbox.credentials to false to block sandboxed commands from reading credential files and secret environment variables
Use this setting to enhance security when running untrusted code in a sandboxed environment

items.title: Added org-configured model restrictions to the model picker, --model, /model, and ANTHROPIC_MODEL, with a "restricted by your organization's…

explanation.what_it_is: Org-configured model restrictions have been added to the model picker, command line flags --model and /model, and the ANTHROPIC_MODEL environment variable. These restrictions are now clearly labeled as 'restricted by your organization' when they apply.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change allows organizations to control which models their users can access, providing an additional layer of security and compliance. It also gives users clear visibility into which models are restricted by their organization.
how_to_use: Use the model picker to see which models are restricted by your organization
Check the --model and /model command line flags for restricted model notifications
Verify that the ANTHROPIC_MODEL environment variable respects org-configured model restrictions

items.title: Added mouse click support to select menus (permission prompts, /model, /config, etc.) in fullscreen mode

explanation.what_it_is: Mouse click support has been added to select menus in fullscreen mode, allowing users to interact with menus like permission prompts, /model, and /config using their mouse.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update makes it easier to navigate and configure Claude Code in fullscreen mode, reducing the need to switch between mouse and keyboard input.
how_to_use: Click on menu options in permission prompts to grant or deny access
Use your mouse to select models in the /model menu
Configure settings in the /config menu with mouse clicks

items.title: Added claude mcp login <name> and claude mcp logout <name> to authenticate MCP servers from the CLI without opening the interactive /mcp menu, with…

explanation.what_it_is: Two new CLI commands, 'claude mcp login <name>' and 'claude mcp logout <name>', allow users to authenticate MCP servers directly from the command line without needing to open the interactive /mcp menu.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change streamlines the workflow for users who need to frequently log in and out of MCP servers, saving time and reducing the number of steps required to manage server connections.
how_to_use: Use 'claude mcp login <name>' to authenticate with an MCP server from the CLI
Use 'claude mcp logout <name>' to log out of an MCP server from the CLI

items.title: Added status filtering (press f) to the /workflows agent detail view

explanation.what_it_is: A new status filtering feature in the /workflows agent detail view, accessible by pressing the 'f' key, allowing users to filter agents by their status.
explanation.why_it_matters: This feature enables Claude Code users to quickly narrow down the list of agents to those with a specific status, streamlining workflow management and troubleshooting.
how_to_use: Press 'f' in the /workflows agent detail view to toggle status filtering
Select a status filter to view only agents with that status

items.title: Added a "Skills" section to the /plugin Installed tab

explanation.what_it_is: A new 'Skills' section has been added to the Installed tab in the /plugin section of Claude Code, which provides information about the capabilities of installed plugins.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change allows users to easily view and understand the skills and capabilities of their installed plugins, making it simpler to manage and utilize them effectively.
how_to_use: Navigate to the /plugin Installed tab to view the new Skills section
Use the Skills section to identify the specific capabilities of each installed plugin

items.title: Added teammateMode: "iterm2" setting with a warning when auto mode cannot find the it2 CLI

explanation.what_it_is: The teammateMode setting now has an 'iterm2' option, which allows Claude Code to integrate with the iTerm2 terminal emulator. This setting also includes a warning when auto mode fails to detect the it2 command-line interface.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update matters because it enables Claude Code users to explicitly configure their integration with iTerm2, potentially resolving issues with auto-detection. The warning for missing it2 CLI also helps users troubleshoot configuration problems.
how_to_use: Set teammateMode to 'iterm2' in your Claude Code settings to use the iTerm2 integration.
Verify that the it2 CLI is installed and accessible to avoid warnings when using auto mode.

items.title: Added "Claude Platform on AWS - refresh credentials" option to /login when awsAuthRefresh is configured

explanation.what_it_is: A new option to refresh AWS credentials when logging in to the Claude Platform, available when awsAuthRefresh is configured.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update allows users to easily renew their AWS credentials without having to reconfigure their setup, streamlining the login process for Claude Platform on AWS.
how_to_use: Go to the /login page with awsAuthRefresh configured to see the 'Claude Platform on AWS - refresh credentials' option
Select the option to refresh your AWS credentials and complete the login process

items.title: Added a warning when the requested model is deprecated or automatically updated to a newer model, shown on stderr in print mode (-p) and now also…

explanation.what_it_is: A warning is now displayed when a requested model is deprecated or has been automatically updated to a newer version.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change helps Claude Code users stay informed about model updates and deprecations, allowing them to adjust their workflows accordingly.
how_to_use: Run Claude Code with the print mode flag (-p) to see the warning on stderr.
Check the warning to determine if your requested model has been updated or deprecated.

items.title: Added attribution.sessionUrl setting to omit the claude.ai session link from commits and PRs in web and Remote Control sessions

explanation.what_it_is: The attribution.sessionUrl setting allows you to control whether the Claude Code session link is included in commits and pull requests. This setting applies to both web and Remote Control sessions.
explanation.why_it_matters: This setting gives you more control over the information included in your commits and PRs, which can be useful for maintaining a clean and organized project history.
how_to_use: Set attribution.sessionUrl to false to omit the session link from commits and PRs
Use this setting in web sessions to keep your project history free of unnecessary links
Apply this setting in Remote Control sessions to maintain consistency with your web session settings

items.title: Added /config --help to list all available shorthand keys for /config key=value

explanation.what_it_is: The /config command now supports a --help option, which lists all available shorthand keys for configuring key-value pairs.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update makes it easier for users to discover and use the available shorthand keys, streamlining their configuration workflow.
how_to_use: Run /config --help to view a list of all supported shorthand keys
Use the listed shorthand keys to configure key-value pairs, e.g., /config k=v

items.title: Added /config key=value syntax to set any setting from the prompt (e.g. /config thinking=false) — works in interactive, -p, and Remote Control

explanation.what_it_is: The /config key=value syntax allows you to set any Claude Code setting directly from the prompt. This syntax can be used in interactive mode, with the -p flag, or in Remote Control.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update gives you more flexibility and control over your Claude Code settings, as you can now change them on the fly without having to navigate through menus or configuration files. This can streamline your workflow and reduce the time spent on configuration.
how_to_use: /config thinking=false to disable thinking mode
/config verbose=true to enable verbose output
/config timeout=300 to set a 5-minute timeout

items.title: Added sandbox.allowAppleEvents opt-in setting that lets sandboxed commands send Apple Events on macOS

explanation.what_it_is: The sandbox.allowAppleEvents setting is an opt-in feature that allows sandboxed commands in Claude Code to send Apple Events on macOS, enabling interaction with other applications on the system.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update matters because it gives developers more control over how their sandboxed commands interact with the macOS environment, allowing for more complex automation workflows.
how_to_use: Enable the sandbox.allowAppleEvents setting in your Claude Code configuration to allow a sandboxed command to send Apple Events to other macOS applications.
Use this setting to automate tasks that require interaction with other applications on the system, such as scripting or automation workflows.

items.title: Added CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE environment variable: point it at a marker file to suppress mobile push notifications while you're at the machine

explanation.what_it_is: The CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE environment variable allows you to specify a marker file that indicates your presence at a machine, which can be used to suppress mobile push notifications.
explanation.why_it_matters: This feature matters because it enables you to avoid receiving redundant mobile push notifications when you're already actively working on a machine, reducing notification noise and potential distractions.
how_to_use: Set the CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE environment variable to point to a marker file on your machine, such as a hidden file in your home directory.
Ensure the marker file is updated or touched when you're actively using the machine, so that Claude Code can detect your presence and suppress mobile push notifications.

items.title: Added Tool(param:value) syntax for permission rules to match a tool's input parameters (with * wildcard), e.g. Agent(model:opus) to block Opus…

explanation.what_it_is: The Tool(param:value) syntax allows you to specify permission rules based on a tool's input parameters, with support for wildcard matching using the * character.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update enables more fine-grained control over tool permissions, allowing you to block or allow specific tools based on their input parameters.
how_to_use: Use Agent(model:opus) to block the Opus model
Use Tool(param:*) to match any tool with a specific parameter

items.title: We've retired the Claude Sonnet 4 model (claude-sonnet-4-20250514) and the…
items.summary: We've retired the Claude Sonnet 4 model (claude-sonnet-4-20250514) and the Claude Opus 4 model (claude-opus-4-20250514). All requests to these models will now return an error. We recommend upgrading…

explanation.why_it_matters: This change requires users to upgrade to newer models to continue using the Claude API, as the retired models are no longer supported.
how_to_use: Update your API requests to use the latest available models
Check the Anthropic API documentation for recommended replacement models

items.title: The code execution tool now supports code_execution_20260521, which discloses…
items.summary: The code execution tool now supports code_execution_20260521, which discloses the 90-second per-cell execution time limit in the tool description so Claude can budget long-running cells. No beta…

explanation.what_it_is: The code execution tool now supports a feature that discloses the 90-second per-cell execution time limit, allowing Claude to manage long-running cells more effectively.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update helps Claude Code users avoid unexpected timeouts and plan their code execution more efficiently by providing clear information about the execution time limits.
how_to_use: Check the tool description for the 90-second per-cell execution time limit when planning code execution
Use this information to budget time for long-running cells and avoid timeouts

items.title: The web search tool and web fetch tool now support web_search_20260318 and…
items.summary: The web search tool and web fetch tool now support web_search_20260318 and web_fetch_20260318, adding a response_inclusion parameter to drop consumed result blocks from the API response for agentic…

explanation.what_it_is: The web search and web fetch tools in the Anthropic API now support models web_search_20260318 and web_fetch_20260318, which include a response_inclusion parameter to control the inclusion of consumed result blocks in API responses.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update allows Claude Code users to reduce the amount of data returned in API responses, potentially improving performance and reducing unnecessary data processing.
how_to_use: Use the response_inclusion parameter to exclude consumed result blocks from API responses for more efficient data handling.
Test the new models web_search_20260318 and web_fetch_20260318 to see how they impact your specific use cases.

items.title: The GET /v1/environments/{id}/work endpoint, which lists pending work for a…
items.summary: The GET /v1/environments/{id}/work endpoint, which lists pending work for a self-hosted sandbox, is now available on Claude Platform on AWS. See IAM actions for Claude Platform on AWS for the…

explanation.what_it_is: The GET /v1/environments/{id}/work endpoint is an API call that lists pending work for a self-hosted sandbox on Claude Platform.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update allows Claude Code users to programmatically retrieve pending work for their self-hosted sandboxes on AWS, enabling better workflow automation and monitoring.
how_to_use: Use the GET /v1/environments/{id}/work endpoint to fetch pending work items for a specific sandbox environment
Integrate this endpoint into your workflow automation scripts to track and manage pending work on AWS

items.title: We've launched Claude Fable 5 (claude-fable-5), our most capable widely…
items.summary: We've launched Claude Fable 5 (claude-fable-5), our most capable widely released model, alongside Claude Mythos 5 (claude-mythos-5) for Project Glasswing participants. Both models support a 1M token…

explanation.what_it_is: Claude Fable 5 is a widely released model that supports up to 1M tokens, offering increased capability for Claude Code users. It is launched alongside Claude Mythos 5, which is available for Project Glasswing participants.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update matters because it provides Claude Code users with access to a more capable model, allowing them to process and generate larger amounts of text. This can be particularly useful for tasks that require longer input or output sequences.
how_to_use: Use Claude Fable 5 to generate longer-form content, such as articles or stories, by providing a prompt and allowing the model to produce up to 1M tokens of output.
Take advantage of the increased token limit to fine-tune the model on larger datasets, potentially leading to improved performance on specific tasks.

items.title: Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 use the tokenizer introduced with Claude…
items.summary: Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 use the tokenizer introduced with Claude Opus 4.7. Compared to models before Claude Opus 4.7, the same text produces roughly 30% more tokens. Use the token counting…

explanation.what_it_is: The tokenizer from Claude Opus 4.7 is now used in Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5, which increases the number of tokens produced for the same text by about 30%.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change affects how you count tokens for these models, as the same input text will now consume more tokens than it did with previous models.
how_to_use: Use the token counting tool to get an accurate count of tokens for your input text with Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5.
Adjust your token budgets accordingly to account for the increased token count.

items.title: Claude Fable 5 runs safety classifiers on requests and during response…
items.summary: Claude Fable 5 runs safety classifiers on requests and during response generation. When a classifier declines a request, the Messages API returns stop_reason: "refusal". You are not billed for a…

explanation.what_it_is: Claude Fable 5 now runs safety classifiers on both incoming requests and during the generation of responses, allowing for more controlled and safe interactions.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update changes how developers interact with the API, as requests that are deemed unsafe will be declined and return a 'refusal' stop reason, and users won't be billed for such declined requests.
how_to_use: Check the Messages API response for 'stop_reason: refusal' to handle declined requests
Use this feature to ensure compliance with safety guidelines in your application

items.title: The stop_details.category field on refusal responses now includes…
items.summary: The stop_details.category field on refusal responses now includes "reasoning_extraction" on Claude Fable 5, returned when a request is blocked under Anthropic's Terms of Service restrictions on…

explanation.what_it_is: The stop_details.category field on refusal responses in Claude Code now includes 'reasoning_extraction' when a request is blocked due to Anthropic's Terms of Service restrictions.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change allows developers to better understand why their requests are being blocked, specifically when it's related to reasoning extraction on Claude Fable 5.
how_to_use: Check the stop_details.category field in refusal responses to identify when a request is blocked due to reasoning extraction restrictions.
Use this information to adjust your requests and ensure compliance with Anthropic's Terms of Service.

items.title: On Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5, adaptive thinking is the only thinking…
items.summary: On Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5, adaptive thinking is the only thinking mode: thinking: {"type": "disabled"} is not supported, and manual extended thinking budgets and assistant prefill are not…

explanation.what_it_is: On Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5, adaptive thinking is now the sole thinking mode, with manual thinking mode and extended thinking budgets no longer supported.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change means Claude Code users must rely on adaptive thinking for these models, simplifying the configuration process but limiting fine-grained control over thinking modes.
how_to_use: Use the default adaptive thinking mode for Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 without specifying a thinking mode
Remove any existing manual thinking mode configurations for these models to ensure compatibility

items.title: On Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5, thinking.display defaults to "omitted",…
items.summary: On Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5, thinking.display defaults to "omitted", the same as Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Opus 4.7, and Claude Mythos Preview; set display: "summarized" to receive readable…

explanation.what_it_is: The thinking.display default setting is now 'omitted' on Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5, meaning that intermediate thinking steps are not shown by default.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change affects how much information is displayed in the output, potentially making it less verbose but also less informative for debugging or understanding the model's thought process.
how_to_use: Set display: 'summarized' to receive a readable summary of the thinking steps.
Use the default 'omitted' setting when you only need the final output and want to reduce verbosity.

items.title: Claude Fable 5 requires 30-day data retention on the Claude API and is not…
items.summary: Claude Fable 5 requires 30-day data retention on the Claude API and is not available under zero data retention. See Model-specific data retention requirements.

explanation.what_it_is: Claude Fable 5 requires that all data exchanged with the Claude API be stored for at least 30 days, which is a change from previous models that allowed for zero data retention.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change affects Claude Code users who need to ensure their applications comply with the new data retention requirement to use Claude Fable 5, potentially impacting data storage and management practices.
how_to_use: Review your application's data storage settings to ensure compliance with the 30-day retention requirement
Update your data management workflows to account for the new retention period

items.title: Claude Managed Agents now supports scheduled deployments, letting you run…
items.summary: Claude Managed Agents now supports scheduled deployments, letting you run sessions on a cron schedule without managing your own scheduler.

explanation.what_it_is: Claude Managed Agents now allows you to schedule deployments using a cron schedule, eliminating the need to manage your own scheduler.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update saves you time and effort by automating the process of running sessions at specific intervals, such as daily or weekly, without requiring manual intervention or a separate scheduling tool.
how_to_use: Set up a cron schedule to run a session daily at 8am
Configure a weekly session to run every Sunday at 12am
Use the scheduled deployment feature to automate recurring tasks, such as data imports or report generation

items.title: Claude Managed Agents vaults now support environment variable credentials, so…
items.summary: Claude Managed Agents vaults now support environment variable credentials, so you can securely inject secrets into the agent's sandbox for CLIs, SDKs, and other services that authenticate through…

explanation.why_it_matters: This update enables Claude Code users to authenticate with CLIs, SDKs, and other services that require credentials, without having to hardcode sensitive information.

Configure the agent's sandbox to use environment variable credentials for services that require authentication

items.title: The session.thread_* webhook events now include a session_thread_id field…

explanation.why_it_matters: This addition allows Claude Code users to more accurately track and manage conversations involving multiple agents, enabling better event handling and logging.
how_to_use: Use the session_thread_id field to correlate related events and maintain conversation context
Update event handlers to parse and utilize the new session_thread_id field for improved logging and analytics

items.title: We've released a Swift package in beta that adds Claude as a server-side…

Use the Swift package to integrate Claude with other Apple Foundation Models framework components.

items.title: We announced the deprecation of the Claude Opus 4.1 model…
items.summary: We announced the deprecation of the Claude Opus 4.1 model (claude-opus-4-1-20250805), with retirement on the Claude API scheduled for August 5, 2026. We recommend migrating to Claude Opus 4.8. Read…

explanation.what_it_is: The Claude Opus 4.1 model is being deprecated, with a scheduled retirement on the Claude API for August 5, 2026.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change requires users to migrate to a newer model, such as Claude Opus 4.8, to avoid disruptions to their workflows after the retirement date.

Review and test workflows that rely on the deprecated model to ensure compatibility with the new model

items.title: The advisor tool now supports a max_tokens parameter to cap the advisor model's…
items.summary: The advisor tool now supports a max_tokens parameter to cap the advisor model's output per call, reducing latency and output token cost for workloads that don't need full-length advisor responses.…

explanation.what_it_is: The advisor tool's max_tokens parameter limits the advisor model's output length per call, allowing for more controlled responses.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change reduces latency and output token cost for workloads that don't require full-length advisor responses, making it more efficient for specific use cases.

Use max_tokens to optimize output token cost for large-scale workloads with limited response length requirements

items.title: On the Claude API, you are no longer billed for a request when it returns…
items.summary: On the Claude API, you are no longer billed for a request when it returns stop_reason: "refusal" without Claude having generated any output. See Streaming refusals for detecting and handling refusals.

Orchestrate multiple agents to work together on complex tasks, using the new multi-agent orchestration features

items.title: We've launched Claude Opus 4.8 (claude-opus-4-8), our most capable generally…
items.summary: We've launched Claude Opus 4.8 (claude-opus-4-8), our most capable generally available model. Claude Opus 4.8 supports a 1M token context window by default on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, and…

Leverage Amazon Bedrock integration for large-scale applications with extended context windows

items.title: We've launched mid-conversation system messages
items.summary: We've launched mid-conversation system messages. On Claude Opus 4.8, you can send role: "system" messages after a user turn (subject to placement rules) in the messages array, preserving prompt cache…

items.title: The stop_details field on refusal responses is now publicly documented; it…

Explicitly set the effort parameter if a different setting is required for a specific use case.

items.title: On Claude Opus 4.8, the minimum cacheable prompt length for prompt caching is…
items.summary: On Claude Opus 4.8, the minimum cacheable prompt length for prompt caching is 1,024 tokens, lower than on Claude Opus 4.7.

Test your application's performance with the updated minimum cacheable prompt length to identify potential optimization opportunities

items.title: With adaptive thinking enabled, Claude Opus 4.8 triggers reasoning only when a…

Monitor your thinking token usage to see the reduction in waste compared to previous versions.

items.title: We've added model capability fields to the Models API
items.summary: We've added model capability fields to the Models API. GET /v1/models and GET /v1/models/{model_id} now return max_input_tokens, max_tokens, and a capabilities object. Query the API to discover what…

explanation.what_it_is: The Models API now includes model capability fields, providing information on max_input_tokens, max_tokens, and a capabilities object for each model. This information is available through the GET /v1/models and GET /v1/models/{model_id} endpoints.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update allows Claude Code users to programmatically discover the capabilities of each model, enabling more informed decisions when selecting models for specific tasks. It also simplifies the process of checking model limitations, such as input token limits.
how_to_use: Use the GET /v1/models endpoint to retrieve a list of models with their corresponding capabilities, including max_input_tokens and max_tokens.
Query the GET /v1/models/{model_id} endpoint to get detailed information about a specific model's capabilities, allowing for more targeted model selection.

items.summary: The 1M token context window is now generally available for Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 at standard pricing. Requests over 200k tokens work automatically for these models with no beta header…

explanation.what_it_is: The 1M token context window allows Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 models to process and respond to input sequences of up to 1 million tokens. This increases the amount of text that can be considered when generating responses.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change enables Claude Code users to handle longer input sequences without needing to truncate or split the text, which can improve the accuracy and coherence of generated responses. It also simplifies the API usage by removing the need for a beta header for requests over 200k tokens.
how_to_use: Send requests with input sequences of up to 1 million tokens to Claude Opus 4.6 or Sonnet 4.6 models without using a beta header
Use the increased context window to process longer documents or conversations

Update your application or workflow to handle the new unified rate limits.
